questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

There was an gang of thieves spotted at our local bank, make sure to be careful.
questions.s:
The error lies in the segment "There was an gang." The article "an" is incorrect before "gang," as "gang" starts with a consonant sound (/ɡ/), requiring the article "a." The correct phrase is "There was a gang." Additionally, the sentence has a structural issue with the second clause ("make sure to be careful"), which lacks a conjunction or proper punctuation (e.g., a semicolon), but this is not part of the options provided.

· Option 1 ("at our local bank") is correct as a prepositional phrase.

· Option 2 ("make sure to be careful") is grammatically correct, though the sentence structure could be improved.

· Option 3 ("There was an gang") contains the article error.

· Option 4 ("of thieves spotted") is correct as a prepositional phrase.

Thus, the segment with the error is There was an gang.

questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The judge adjourn the court proceedings until further notice.
questions.s:
The part that contains the error is 'adjourn'. The error lies in the subject-verb agreement. The subject of the sentence is "judge," which is singular. But the verb "adjourn" is plural. The verb needs to be conjugated correctly for the singular subject. Therefore, to correct the error, the plural verb 'adjourn' should be replaced with the singular verb 'adjourns' to match the singular subject "judge". Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Or simply, replace 'adjourn' with its past form 'adjourned' to rectify the error.

The correct sentence is: The judge adjourns the court proceedings until further notice.

Or

The judge adjourned the court proceedings until further notice.

NOTE:

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The farmer watched his ________ of cattle grazing in the lush field.
questions.s:
The context of the sentence involves a group of a specific type of animal, "cattle". The blank requires the correct collective noun used for a group of cattle.

The correct option is "herd". A "herd of cattle" is the standard and correct collective noun for this group of animals.

The other options are incorrect collective nouns for cattle: a "flock" is used for sheep or birds; a "school" is used for fish or whales; a "pride" is used for lions.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "The farmer watched his herd of cattle grazing in the lush field."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note: Collective Noun: It is the name given to a number (or collection) of persons or things taken together and spoken of as one whole. Examples could be crowd, fleet, committee, family, army, jury, heard, etc.
